composition: Use a 10:1 or 14:1 ultra-wide horizontal strip layout.
Symmetrical layout: Center 10-20% reserved for logo, flanked by secondary text/links at 30% and 70% marks.
Asymmetrical layout: Left 30% for character cutout/branding, center 40% for text, right 30% for call-to-action or graphics.
Frame outer edges with dark, desaturated silhouettes (e.g., palm trees) to create depth.
typographie: Primary title: Bold, italicized sans-serif in all-caps, sized to 60-70% of the vertical height.
Secondary links/URLs: Clean, geometric, widely spaced (tracked-out) lowercase sans-serif at 15-20% vertical height.
Apply high-contrast color-coding (e.g., white base text paired with a single vibrant accent color like mint green or hot pink).
lumiere: Low-key ambient lighting with a strong, localized neon under-glow radiating from the bottom-center.
Soft, diffused backlighting behind the central logo to create a halo separation effect.
Vignetted edges fading to near-black to draw focus to the center.
etalonnage: Monochromatic dark base (charcoal, deep navy, or black) paired with one high-saturation accent hue.
Dominant accent families: Crimson Red (#800000), Hot Pink (#FF69B4), Mint Green (#00FF99), or Deep Purple.
Low midtone contrast for a cinematic, gritty, or synthwave-inspired atmosphere.
effets: Subtle background textures: diagonal scanlines, fine dust particles, or a soft grunge overlay.
Soft depth-of-field blur on background elements (e.g., snowflakes, foliage) to separate layers.
Soft outer glows on text and interactive UI elements like pill buttons.
logo: Position logo strictly in the dead center (middle 10-20%) or on the far left (0-30% zone) as a clean monogram.
interdits: Do not use overly dark, compressed background silhouettes that turn into muddy noise.
Avoid clashing font styles (e.g., pairing a moody, mature aesthetic with playful, rounded lowercase fonts).
Do not scale call-to-action button text too small (must remain legible at low resolutions).
Avoid perfectly mirrored, repetitive background assets on the flanks.
Do not use highly specific seasonal motifs (like Santa hats) that limit year-round usability.
